mark_affecting.quote: Then Maggie insists he learn to read and write. We get these comic, but honestly really touching scenes of him struggling with his letters... Finally... he hits this moment of immense pride realizing his name wrote up on the windows.

flagged.title: Acts 3-4: The Power Shift
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly places Hobson's fall and medical diagnosis in Act 3 rather than Acts 2 and 4, claims the fall occurs on stage when it is reported offstage, and wrongly attributes demanding the 'Mossop & Hobson' sign to Maggie instead of Willie.

mark_affecting.quote: But by the time we hit Act 3, he is a humiliated dependent... And how does this downfall actually happen? Like physically, through a literal fall... a totally intoxicated Hobson tumbles right through the cellar trapdoor
We also need to pause and talk about why he fell. A doctor actually diagnoses Hobson with chronic alcoholism, warning him that he has to stop drinking
Her condition for saving her father is absolute: Willie is going to become the master of the shop, and the new sign over the door will read 'Mossop & Hobson'.

mark_affecting.video_says: His physical collapse on stage is literally mirroring the complete collapse of his authority and business.
mark_affecting.lesson_says: The fall itself happens offstage: Fred Beenstock brings the news
